questions.question: When should you give up your right-of-way?

options.text: Often, even at controlled intersections.
Whenever it helps prevent crashes.
Never. It confuses other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Whenever it helps prevent crashes.
questions.explanation: Do not assume other drivers will let you go first. Give up your right-of-way whenever it helps prevent crashes.

questions.question: When should you increase the distance between your vehicle and the car ahead?

options.text: When following a small passenger car.
When another driver is tailgating you.
When you are driving slower than the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: When another driver is tailgating you.
questions.explanation: When someone is tailgating you, leave extra space in front of your vehicle. Slow down gradually or change lanes. Do not brake suddenly. This helps prevent a crash with the tailgater.

questions.question: What does a steady yellow X on a reversible lane signal mean?

options.text: The signal is about to change to a red X.
The signal is about to change to a green arrow.
You can drive normally in this lane.
You can drive slowly in this lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The signal is about to change to a red X.
questions.explanation: Lane control signals show which lanes are open or closed. They change throughout the day as traffic direction changes. A steady yellow X means leave this lane now. The signal will soon change to a red X.

questions.question: When can you cross solid yellow lines?

options.text: To pass traffic moving in the same direction.
During daylight hours only.
At any time.
When making turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: When making turns.
questions.explanation: Broken lines can be crossed. Solid lines cannot be crossed, except when you are making a turn.

questions.question: Highways and roads freeze before ramps and bridges.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: Ramps and bridges freeze first. They hang in the air, so they get icy quickly in cold weather. Drive carefully when crossing a bridge in freezing temperatures.

questions.question: What does a green arrow on a reversible lane signal mean?

options.text: The signal is about to change to a red X.
You should not drive in this lane.
You can only turn left in this lane.
You can drive normally in this lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can drive normally in this lane.
questions.explanation: Lane control signals show which lanes are open or closed. They change throughout the day as traffic direction changes. A green arrow means the lane is open and you can drive normally in it.

questions.question: What color are road markings that separate traffic lanes moving in opposite directions?

options.text: Yellow
White
Yellow and white
Yellow, white, and black

questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow
questions.explanation: Yellow lines in the center of the road separate traffic moving in opposite directions.

questions.question: What does NOT affect how far a vehicle needs to stop?

options.text: Your reaction time.
The time of day.
Your vehicle's brake condition.
Your vehicle's tire condition and type.

questions.correctAnswerText: The time of day.
questions.explanation: Stopping distance depends on your reaction time, weather and visibility, vehicle weight, brake condition, tire condition and type, road conditions, and speed. The time of day does not matter.

questions.question: What do you do at an intersection with a flashing red light?

options.text: Stop completely, let traffic and pedestrians go, then go.
Slow down and continue with caution.
Stop and stay stopped until the light turns green.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, let traffic and pedestrians go, then go.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. Stop fully. Make sure the road is clear, then go when it is safe.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?

options.text: Turn left.
Turn right.
Stop.
Go straight ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn right.
questions.explanation: When a driver's left arm points straight up, it means they are turning right. If you are following this driver, adjust your speed and direction accordingly.

questions.question: How do you avoid hydroplaning while driving in rain?

options.text: Drive at the speed you would use in good weather.
Apply your brakes as soon as your car starts to skid.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: When you drive too fast in wet conditions, your tires can lose contact with the road. Your car will ride on top of the water instead of gripping the road. This is called hydroplaning. Driving slowly in rain prevents this.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line mean?

options.text: You can pass from either direction.
You can pass from the lane with the broken line.
You can pass from the lane with the solid line.
You cannot pass from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass from the lane with the broken line.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means passing is allowed only from the side with the broken line.

questions.question: When parking uphill next to a curb, set the parking brake and:

options.text: Keep the rear tires against the curb.
Keep the front tires straight.
Turn your steering wheel away from the curb.
Turn your steering wheel toward the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your steering wheel away from the curb.
questions.explanation: When parking facing uphill, set the parking brake and turn the wheel away from the curb. If the car rolls, it will roll toward the curb and stop.

questions.question: When stopping on snow or ice with an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS), you should:

options.text: Pump the brakes.
Press and hold the brake pedal firmly.
Stay off the brakes and let the car slow down on its own.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press and hold the brake pedal firmly.
questions.explanation: With ABS, press the brake pedal hard and keep it pressed. The ABS will pump the brakes faster than you can.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Watch for trucks.
Do not pass trucks.
Truck parking area ahead.
Steep downgrade ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steep downgrade ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a steep hill is coming.

questions.question: If your car starts to skid, you should:

options.text: Brake lightly.
Stay off the brakes.
Brake hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay off the brakes.
questions.explanation: Do not use the brakes during a skid. Braking will make the skid worse.

questions.question: A solid white line on the right edge of the road angles toward the center. What does this mean?

options.text: There is an intersection just ahead.
You are approaching a construction area.
You must turn left just ahead.
The road will get narrower.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road will get narrower.
questions.explanation: A solid edge line marks the boundary of the road. When it angles toward the center, the road is getting narrower.

questions.question: Which of these helps direct drivers into the correct turning lanes on highways?

options.text: Flashing red lights
Flashing yellow lights
White lines on the side of the road
White arrows painted in the lanes

questions.correctAnswerText: White arrows painted in the lanes
questions.explanation: Arrows in lanes show drivers which lanes to use for going straight or turning.

questions.question: What is a speed restriction sign?

options.text: You can ignore it in rain, snow, or ice.
It has a triangular shape.
It is blue with black lettering.
It shows a recommended speed for curves or turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: It shows a recommended speed for curves or turns.
questions.explanation: Speed signs on curves and turns show a recommended safe speed. You should follow this speed even if you think you can go faster in good weather. Never go faster in rain, snow, or ice.

questions.question: When turning left onto a one-way street, you should turn into:

options.text: The right lane.
The lane closest to where you came from.
Either lane.
Neither lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane closest to where you came from.
questions.explanation: Always turn into the lane that is closest to your previous lane of travel.
